items.title: Lovie Austin Interview, 1969-04-25
items.q: The interviewee mentions Jolly Row Martin only in the context of the interviewer knowing him ('I knew, well, that's one place where I'd met Jolly Row Martin'). The interviewee does not claim to have met, worked with, or known Jolly Row Martin personally.

ctx.x: You probably knew my father, because he was a great musician and a teacher in New York. Did you know Professor Calvin?

No, I wasn't around New York very long, actually, and I didn't get to meet many musicians there. Although I did know, for instance, as I say, Tommy Ladner, and I knew, well, that's one place where I'd met Jolly Row Martin in Washington, and he came to, just the last couple of years of his life is when I knew him, only 1938 when I met him, and he died in 41.

Well, I went to work at the Monogram in 1913. In 13? And I worked at 34th Street until they moved to 35th Street, and I moved there with him. That's the first time I went to New York, and I came right back and stayed down there when I worked there 25 years straight. And then I went to New York and started working for Herdic and Seaman. I was taking high fast shows, and I worked for Herdic and Seaman for a long time. And then I came, when I came home, my mother died in 31. So I just came on the stage. You stayed…
